Ben Ortiz: run three benchmark runs (50k tokens total) on dedicated instance and upload results to shared sheet (due 2025-12-10)
Jordan Lee: send SOC2 summary, KMS/HSM notes, and SAML/SSO integration guide (due 2025-12-05)

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about an hour on the calendar for our weekly POC sync. quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha (FinMuse): Hey, Aisha here.
[00:10] Ben (FinMuse): Ben, hey.
[00:12] Ravi (FinMuse): Ravi here.
[00:15] Samir (Redwood SE): Samir from Redwood, thanks.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool. real quick agenda - review last week's integration progress, SDK tool/function calls and structured output changes, any blockers, security ask, and next steps.
[00:30] Aisha: We pushed the SDK into our staging - mostly straightforward, thanks - but we hit a snag with tool-calls where the function schema wasn't being enforced and sometimes the response was plain text instead of JSON.
[00:45] Samir: ok that sounds like the function signature/contract didn't match what the runtime expected. can you show the snippet you used?
[00:53] Ben: yeah i'll paste in the sheet after but quick note - we're calling from a node microservice behind our VPC, using the simple-post integration. we saw a few 502s when the payload was large, maybe kv cash issues?
[01:10] Jordan: KV cash? you mean KV cache, right - yeah the transcript sometimes says cash -
[01:15] Ben: yes KV cache, sorry.
[01:17] Samir: ok two separate things: 1) SDK usage - we updated the snippet to include the 'function' block with explicit parameter schema and 'response_format' set to "json"; 2) for the 502s, that smells like request size or a transient routing/timeout from within the staging subnet.
[01:40] Aisha: the SDK snippet from last week used the high-level call: redwood.generate({ model: 'rw-medium-13b', prompt, functions: [...] }) - we saw that when the structured output had optional fields the runtime returned plain text.
[01:55] Samir: yeah we have an opt-in strict structured-output mode. if you pass response_format: "strict_json" we run a schema validation step and will return a structured error if validation fails instead of falling back to text. it's off by default to reduce latency overhead.
[02:15] Ravi: that's helpful - what's the latency overhead on strict_json?
[02:20] Samir: in our last internal tests, strict validation added roughly 30-80ms median depending on payload size, worst-case ~200ms on large payloads. again that's internal, but should give a ballpark.
[02:35] Ben: fines, 30-80ms is acceptable. our SLA target is P95 < 500ms for user-facing calls.
[02:40] Jordan: good note - i'll flag that as success criteria.
[02:45] Aisha: about tool calls - we're also chaining a small internal search tool after generation (tool returns doc ids), then we do a rerank with embeddings. any recommended pattern for latency/cost?
[02:58] Samir: two patterns: synchronous tool-call where the LLM returns tool args and you call tool inline; or async where you return a placeholder and kickoff the tool after output. sync is simpler but adds latency; async reduces user-facing latency but complicates flow. for rerank, consider using Redwood embeddings API with cached vectors in your vector DB - we also suggest batching rerank calls if you can tolerate a small delay.
[03:30] Ben: got it, we'll try batching.
[03:35] Jordan: ok, any blockers on integration?
[03:37] Aisha: only the strict_json and a few auth bits - we need SSO/SAML for production, and confirm KMS for keys.
[03:45] Jordan: on SSO, we have a SAML guide, and for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. i'll send the docs.
[03:55] Ravi: security is a must for procurement. also curious about audit logs retention - can we get per-call traces?
[04:02] Samir: yes audit logs include per-request metadata (model, route, token counts, latency), and we can provision longer retention under the enterprise add-on. logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM.
[04:12] Ben: sweet. sorry returning to the earlier issue, the 502s - payloads are around 2.1MB sometimes with attachments, is there a hard limit?
[04:23] Samir: generally we recommend sub-1MB for lowest latency; larger payloads increase request time and can trigger timeouts on intermediate proxies. we can increase timeouts for your dedicated trial instance - we'll check the staging network path.
[04:35] Aisha: also on model choice - we began with rw-medium-13b then tried a quantized variant to cut cost. the quantized model was cheaper but showed slight hallucination spikes on numeric tables.
[04:50] Samir: yep quantization tradeoffs are expected. for structured numeric outputs we recommend the unquantized or a higher-precision quant profile; alternatively add post-checks in your structured schema to validate numeric ranges.
[05:05] Ben: can Redwood run a quick eval on our sample prompts to recommend quantization/profile?
[05:10] Jordan: yes we can - Samir can run a mini-eval against your sample set and suggest a profile.
[05:20] Samir: please drop the sample prompt set in the shared folder - i'll kick off the eval and post a short report.
[05:26] Aisha: done, i've uploaded 120 prompts to the POC/benchmarks sheet, note the 'structured output' tab.
[05:32] Jordan: perfect.
[05:35] [10:05] Samir: quick SDK note - earlier you used the Node v0.9 snippet; there's a newer helper which has first-class support for function/tool calling and will automatically do response_format enforcement. i'll paste the updated snippet after the call. one caveat: if you're using older axios proxies inside your VPC you might need to set keepAlive false, some proxies mishandle streaming chunks.
[05:58] Ben: interesting, our infra uses an nginx ingress that has chunked buffering on by default. could that cause the 502s when streaming?
[06:05] Samir: yes, buffering can interfere with streaming/long-lived connections; for now try non-streaming calls for the tool path or tune nginx to disable proxy_buffering for that route.
[06:18] Ravi: and for streaming we saw partial transcripts truncated sometimes, likely due to the same buffering issue.
[06:25] Samir: yep.
[06:27] Jordan: let's list action items: Samir, SDK snippet; Ben run benchmarks; Jordan security docs; Ravi confirm stakeholder list.
[06:35] [20:00] Ben: a question on routing and fallback - if our primary model is down or overloaded can we fallback to a smaller model automatically? we worry about graceful degradation.
[06:45] Samir: Redwood supports routing policies; you can configure a tiered fallback chain: primary model -> smaller compatible variant -> hosted cheap model. fallbacks preserve schema where possible; for drastic changes you can configure a transform to adjust output. there is a small cost to switching, but it's much better than a total outage.
[07:05] Aisha: any observable impact on token unit billing when fallback occurs?
[07:10] Jordan: yes, billing is per-token at the model/route used, so fallback to a cheaper model reduces cost; but mixing models can complicate evals - we'll include per-route cost breakdown in the Console.
[07:22] Ben: good to know.
[07:25] Samir: i also wanted to flag batching/caching knobs: prefix caching for repeated prompts can dramatically reduce tokens and latency; continuous batching can help throughput on dedicated pools. we'll propose config for your traffic pattern after benchmarking.
[07:45] Ravi: what's the recommended batch size for P95 < 500ms?
[07:50] Samir: it depends on sequence length; for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) batching of 8-16 keeps latency low and increases throughput; for longer ones keep batch small. we'll provide suggested autoscale policies.
[08:05] Aisha: procurement wanted to confirm legal - do you have standard DPA and subprocessor list?
[08:10] Jordan: yes we'll attach DPA and current subprocessor list with the security bundle.
[08:14] Ben: one more note - the structured output failures we've seen were intermittent when optional fields were missing; can we get a sample error payload to map to our retry logic?
[08:22] Samir: yes when strict_json is enabled you get an error object with 'schema_path' and 'validation_errors' keys; otherwise you'll get partial text. i'll include example payloads.
[08:35] [45:00] Aisha: overall the integration is promising, performance looks decent in staging aside from the occasional 502. our priorities: 1) stable structured output, 2) SSO/KMS for production, 3) benchmark numbers for procurement.
[08:50] Jordan: sounds good. Ben/Ravi please confirm procurement date - when do you need final numbers?
[08:56] Ravi: target is 2025-12-18 for vendor selection.
[09:00] Jordan: okay we'll aim to have the benchmark and security bundle before then.
[09:05] Samir: i'll also propose a test plan for routing and fallback checks to reproduce tail latency.
[09:12] Ben: thanks.
[09:14] Jordan: wrapping up - recap of next steps and I will email the notes, Samir will drop SDK snippet, Ben will run benchmarks and upload to the shared sheet, Jordan will send security bundle. any final questions?
[09:27] Aisha: none here, thanks everyone.
[09:30] Jordan: thanks all, see you next week.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (KV cash, etc.). Links referenced in call: shared bench sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/finmuse-poc-bench), SDK snippet (will be posted to Slack #finmuse-poc), security bundle link placeholder.
